chose: the COMMAND registry lives in a new src/commands.ts, not in src/cli.ts beside the dispatch
over: src/cli.ts, adjacent to the if/else dispatch it describes
src/render-commands.ts, matching the render-* naming convention
because: cli.ts EXECUTES at import time (top-level process.argv dispatch and process.exit), so a test that imports a registry living there would run the CLI and exit(2) — the totality oracle is the whole point of the exercise and it must be able to import the source of truth. render-* was rejected because the registry and its two derived spellings are the reason the file exists; splitting them buys an import hop and nothing else.

chose: a registry + a totality oracle that reads the LIVE dispatch out of cli.ts's AST, with the banner and the README index derived
over: a Record<name, handler> dispatch table that deletes the correspondence outright instead of checking it
a hand-written expected-command list in the test
because: the handler table is the strongest form and should happen eventually, but cli.ts's dispatch is 350 lines of early exits, shared locals and per-command usage errors: rewriting it to land a documentation fix trades a checked correspondence for an unchecked rewrite. A hand-written expected list was rejected outright — it would be a FOURTH spelling of the same domain and would drift exactly like the other three. The oracle reads the AST rather than a regex because a regex also matches cmd === "x" inside a comment, and an oracle a code comment can fool is not one.

chose: the derived README index is a BULLET LIST, and the scaffold entry's usage reads <kind> rather than spelling its four kinds
over: a markdown table, which reads better as an index
carrying <boundary|component|invariant|parity> through from the old banner line
because: redundancy reads the first column of every markdown table as an enumerated domain, so a generated table hands it a fresh README-vs-dispatch pair — trading the finding this change removes for an identical one, which fixes nothing. Same reasoning one level down for the scaffold kinds: a DERIVED index propagates whatever the registry spells, and README already spelled those four in prose, so carrying them added a pair. Measured: with <kind>, redundancy goes 42 pairs to 37 with ZERO added; carrying the alternation added one new sub-floor pair.

chose: docs --check treats an absent README fence pair as NOT OWNED (green), while claude --check reds on absent markers
over: one uniform rule — red on missing markers for both owned blocks
silently skipping either way, with no output
because: docs runs in every consuming project, and a gate that fails on a file the project never opted into is a gate that gets switched off wholesale; claude is opt-in per invocation, so there a missing marker pair genuinely means the file failed to get wired up. The skip is not SILENT though — the write path prints the marker pair to paste, because a command that exits 0 having done nothing is the exact defect this harness exists to catch.

chose: measured the redundancy acceptance test from an isolated git worktree at b498b7d with node_modules symlinked in
over: git stash push --include-untracked around the measurement
git checkout <ref> -- . to revert in place
because: checkout -- . does NOT delete files absent from the ref, so the baseline ran with b498b7d's cli.ts AND the new src/commands.ts both present and reported a fabricated 39-pair baseline with pairs that exist in neither tree. The stash form is sound but silently mixes measurement with mutation of the tree under test. A worktree cannot be contaminated by the working copy — and it fails LOUDLY rather than quietly when node_modules is missing, which is how the first contaminated number got caught.
